title: A timed-out read prints a resume command that runs exactly as printed and does not time out again
description: A timed-out read prints a resume command that runs exactly as printed and does not time out again
acceptance_criteria: the_resume_command_splits_back_into_the_original_arguments passes: every argument that is not made only of shell-safe characters is single-quoted, so sh splits the printed resume command back into exactly the original arguments, including $, ;, *, an apostrophe, spaces and an empty argument (committed failing first in db16db8a)

With SPECSYNC_TIMEOUT set, the printed resume command starts with SPECSYNC_TIMEOUT= so it runs without the deadline it is resuming from (an_archived_status_past_its_timeout_exits_124_and_names_how_to_resume, extended and failing first in db16db8a)
Without SPECSYNC_TIMEOUT the resume command is unchanged apart from quoting; --timeout and --timeout=<n> are still dropped
The timeout report shape, exit 124 and the cache flush are unchanged

answers.constraints: SPEED-1 (no command keeps an agent waiting minutes); REQ-change-137 and REQ-cmd-change-032 (the timeout report and its exact resume command) stay; Codex P2s #923 and #953 deferred from #918
